svg.title: Figure 10-1. The item boundary in the safety view (WP-C-04 §2, §5, §9, §10)
svg.desc: The item boundary of WP-C-01 Figure 3-2 with the WP-C-04 allocation on each element. E-01: 17 FSRs, highest C, serving SG-01, SG-02, SG-03, SG-04, SG-05, SG-06, SG-07; QM element carrying ASIL FSRs. E-01/DM: 5 FSRs, highest A, serving SG-02, SG-04, SG-06, SG-08; QM element carrying ASIL FSRs. E-01/HMI: 5 FSRs, highest C, serving SG-02, SG-05, SG-06, SG-07, SG-08; QM element carrying ASIL FSRs. E-02: 1 FSRs, highest A, serving SG-02, SG-06, SG-08; QM element carrying ASIL FSRs. E-03: 42 FSRs, highest C, serving SG-01, SG-02, SG-03, SG-04, SG-05, SG-06, SG-07. E-05: 3 FSRs, highest C, serving SG-01, SG-03, SG-07. EXT-EPS: 1 FSRs, highest ext, serving SG-01, SG-05. EXT-PCM: 4 FSRs, highest B, serving SG-03, SG-04, SG-05, SG-07. EXT-CLU: 1 FSRs, highest C, serving SG-02, SG-05, SG-06. Driver: no FSR, assumptions AOU-06R, AOU-02R.

svg.text: Every FSR is Proposed: a box shows allocation, not implementation (§5 Impl). FSR-06.05 is allocated as the FSRs it references and is not counted. ASILs are those of the HARA, not yet confirmed (I3).

g.text: Terms: AEB automatic emergency braking · AoU assumption of use: what the analysis assumes about the car, the driver or the environment · AOU-nn assumption of use (WP-C-01 §7); an R suffix marks the FSC's refined

version · ASIL Automotive Safety Integrity Level, A (lowest) to D (highest), from ISO 26262 · C0–C3 controllability class C0 (controllable in general) to C3 (difficult or uncontrollable) · CAN controller area

network: the vehicle's data bus · DM driver monitoring · DRV the driver · E-nn element of the item (WP-C-01 §3.1), E-01…E-06 · E/E electrical and electronic (systems) · ECM engine control module · EPS electric power

steering · EXT-nn external element credited only through an assumption of use (EXT-EPS, EXT-PCM, EXT-CLU) · FSR-nn functional safety requirement (FSC) · HARA hazard analysis and risk assessment (ISO 26262-3) · HMI

human-machine interface: display, sounds, cluster · I0–I3 independence level of a review, I0 (none, e.g. the author or an AI) to I3 (independent organisation) · IF-nn interface of the item (WP-C-01 §3.4) · LD-SDA

LionDriver Supervised Driving Assistance, the item · MCU microcontroller: the panda safety processor (STM32H7) · ML machine learning · OI-nn open item of the document it appears in · PCM powertrain control module

(engine and drive) · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning and braking · QM quality managed: no ASIL; ordinary quality processes suffice · SG-nn safety goal (HARA §6) · SoC system on chip: the

comma device's main processor, running openpilot (QM) · SPI serial peripheral interface (the link between SoC and MCU) · WP-nn work product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M management, C concept, S system, H
hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
